//| output: true
u5hViz = {
  const reduceMotion = window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches;
  // Taller map on phones, wider on big screens
  const narrow = window.innerWidth < 640;
  const W = narrow ? 600 : 900, H = narrow ? 660 : 540;
  const NYC = [-74.017, 40.703];             // The Battery, Lower Manhattan
  const ST = ["HU", "TS", "TD", "EX", "SS", "SD", "LO", "WV", "DB"];
  const KT2MPH = 1.15078;
  const mph = kt => Math.round(kt * KT2MPH / 5) * 5;
  const cat = kt => kt >= 137 ? 5 : kt >= 113 ? 4 : kt >= 96 ? 3 : kt >= 83 ? 2 : 1;
  const months = ["Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr","May","Jun","Jul","Aug","Sep","Oct","Nov","Dec"];

  // Intensity class for one track point
  const cls = (st, w) => st === "HU" ? (w >= 96 ? "major" : "hu")
    : (st === "TS" || st === "SS") ? "ts"
    : (st === "TD" || st === "SD") ? "td" : "other";
  const COLORS = {major: "#f43f5e", hu: "#fb923c", ts: "#facc15", td: "#38bdf8", other: "#94a3b8"};
  const LABELS = [["major", "Major hurricane (Cat 3–5)"], ["hu", "Hurricane (Cat 1–2)"], ["ts", "Tropical storm"], ["td", "Tropical depression"], ["other", "Post-tropical or remnant"]];
  const describe = (st, w) => st === "HU" ? `<b>Category ${cat(w)} hurricane</b>`
    : st === "TS" ? "<b>tropical storm</b>" : st === "SS" ? "<b>subtropical storm</b>"
    : st === "TD" ? "<b>tropical depression</b>" : st === "SD" ? "<b>subtropical depression</b>"
    : st === "EX" ? "<b>post-tropical storm</b>" : "<b>remnant low</b>";

  const NOTES = {
    "1938": "Hit Long Island as a Category 3 hurricane. People called it the “Long Island Express.”",
    "2011Irene": "Its center passed almost directly over New York City.",
    "2012Sandy": "It was no longer a hurricane here, but its storm surge flooded NYC subway tunnels.",
    "2021Ida": "Its leftover rain caused deadly flash floods in NYC."
  };

  const storms = u5hData.map((s, i) => {
    const pts = d3.range(s.t.length / 4).map(j => ({
      lon: s.t[j * 4], lat: s.t[j * 4 + 1], w: s.t[j * 4 + 2], st: ST[s.t[j * 4 + 3]]
    }));
    // Split the track into runs of the same intensity class
    const runs = [];
    for (let j = 0; j < pts.length - 1; j++) {
      const c = cls(pts[j].st, pts[j].w);
      const last = runs[runs.length - 1];
      if (last && last.c === c) last.coords.push([pts[j + 1].lon, pts[j + 1].lat]);
      else runs.push({c, coords: [[pts[j].lon, pts[j].lat], [pts[j + 1].lon, pts[j + 1].lat]]});
    }
    const trop = pts.filter(p => ["HU", "TS", "TD", "SS", "SD"].includes(p.st));
    const peak = trop.length ? trop.reduce((a, b) => b.w > a.w ? b : a) : pts.reduce((a, b) => b.w > a.w ? b : a);
    const label = s.n ? `${s.n} (${s.y})` : s.y === 1938 ? "The 1938 “Long Island Express” hurricane" : `Unnamed storm (${s.y})`;
    return {...s, i, pts, runs, peak, label, close: pts[s.c], note: NOTES[`${s.y}${s.n}`] || NOTES[s.y === 1938 ? "1938" : ""]};
  });
  const firstYear = 1851, lastYear = 2025;   // HURDAT2 file covers 1851–2025

  // ---------- DOM ----------
  const wrap = html`<div class="u5h-viz"></div>`;
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${W} ${H}`)
    .attr("role", "img")
    .attr("aria-label", `Map of the western Atlantic Ocean and the U.S. East Coast showing the paths of all ${storms.length} storms in NOAA's HURDAT2 hurricane record, from 1851 to ${lastYear}, that passed within 150 kilometers of New York City. Most tracks start in the tropics and curve north along the coast toward NYC. Track colors show storm strength along each path.`);

  const controls = html`<div class="u5h-controls"></div>`;
  const playBtn = html`<button type="button" class="u5h-ctl">▶ Play</button>`;
  const yearBox = html`<label class="u5h-year"><span class="visually-hidden">Show storms up to year</span><input type="range" min=${firstYear} max=${lastYear} step="1" value=${lastYear} aria-label="Show storms up to this year"><output>${lastYear}</output></label>`;
  const slider = yearBox.querySelector("input"), out = yearBox.querySelector("output");
  const zoomBtn = html`<button type="button" class="u5h-ctl" aria-pressed="false">🔍 Zoom to NYC</button>`;
  controls.append(playBtn, yearBox, zoomBtn);

  const count = html`<p class="u5h-count" aria-live="polite"></p>`;
  const picks = html`<div class="u5h-picks" role="group" aria-label="Famous storms"></div>`;
  const famous = [["Sandy", 2012, "Sandy 2012"], ["", 1938, "1938 Long Island Express"], ["Irene", 2011, "Irene 2011"], ["Ida", 2021, "Ida 2021"]];
  const pickBtns = famous.map(([n, y, txt]) => {
    const s = storms.find(d => d.y === y && d.n === n);
    const b = html`<button type="button" class="u5h-ctl">${txt}</button>`;
    b.onclick = () => select(s);
    picks.append(b);
    return b;
  });
  const sel = html`<select class="u5h-select" aria-label="Pick any storm from the list">
    <option value="">Or pick any of the ${storms.length} storms…</option>
    ${storms.slice().sort((a, b) => b.y - a.y).map(s => html`<option value=${s.i}>${s.y} · ${s.n || (s.y === 1938 ? "Long Island Express" : "Unnamed")}</option>`)}
  </select>`;
  sel.onchange = () => select(sel.value === "" ? null : storms[+sel.value]);
  picks.append(sel);

  const read = html`<div class="u5h-read" aria-live="polite"></div>`;
  const legend = html`<div class="u5h-legend" aria-hidden="true">${LABELS.map(([k, t]) => html`<span><i style="background:${COLORS[k]}"></i>${t}</span>`)}<span><i style="background:#fff;height:10px;width:10px;border-radius:50%"></i>NYC, with the 150 km circle</span></div>`;
  wrap.append(svg.node(), controls, count, picks, read, legend);

  // ---------- Map ----------
  const views = {
    atlantic: {type: "MultiPoint", coordinates: narrow ? [[-97, 13], [-56, 13], [-97, 48], [-56, 48]] : [[-99, 12], [-40, 12], [-99, 50], [-40, 50]]},
    nyc: {type: "MultiPoint", coordinates: narrow ? [[-79, 36.5], [-69, 36.5], [-79, 45], [-69, 45]] : [[-82, 36], [-66, 36], [-82, 45.5], [-66, 45.5]]}
  };
  const projection = d3.geoConicConformal().parallels([25, 45]).rotate([70, 0]);
  const path = d3.geoPath(projection);
  const fit = v => projection.fitExtent([[8, 8], [W - 8, H - 8]], views[v]).clipExtent([[0, 0], [W, H]]);
  fit("atlantic");

  const gBase = svg.append("g");
  const gTracks = svg.append("g").attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke-linecap", "round").attr("stroke-linejoin", "round");
  const gTop = svg.append("g").attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke-linecap", "round").attr("stroke-linejoin", "round");
  const gNyc = svg.append("g");
  const gHit = svg.append("g").attr("fill", "none");

  let year = lastYear, selected = null, view = "atlantic";

  function drawBase() {
    gBase.selectAll("*").remove();
    gBase.append("path").attr("d", path(d3.geoGraticule10())).attr("stroke", "rgba(148,163,184,0.14)").attr("fill", "none");
    if (u5hLand) gBase.append("path").attr("d", path(u5hLand)).attr("fill", "#1f4d45").attr("stroke", "rgba(226,232,240,0.35)").attr("stroke-width", 0.6);
    gNyc.selectAll("*").remove();
    gNyc.append("path").attr("d", path(d3.geoCircle().center(NYC).radius(150 / 111.2)()))
      .attr("fill", "rgba(255,255,255,0.06)").attr("stroke", "#fff").attr("stroke-dasharray", "4 4").attr("stroke-width", 1.2);
    const [x, y] = projection(NYC);
    gNyc.append("circle").attr("cx", x).attr("cy", y).attr("r", 5).attr("fill", "#fff").attr("stroke", "#020617").attr("stroke-width", 1.5);
    gNyc.append("text").attr("x", x - 9).attr("y", y - 9).attr("text-anchor", "end")
      .attr("fill", "#fff").attr("font-size", view === "nyc" ? 22 : 20).attr("font-weight", 700)
      .attr("font-family", "Space Grotesk, system-ui, sans-serif")
      .attr("paint-order", "stroke").attr("stroke", "#020617").attr("stroke-width", 4).text("NYC");
  }

  function drawTracks() {
    const shown = storms.filter(s => s.y <= year);
    const dim = selected ? 0.18 : 1;
    gTracks.selectAll("g.u5h-trk").data(shown, d => d.i).join(
      enter => {
        const g = enter.append("g").attr("class", "u5h-trk");
        g.selectAll("path").data(d => d.runs).join("path");
        return g;
      }
    ).each(function (s) {
      const fresh = s.y === year && year !== lastYear;
      d3.select(this).attr("opacity", (fresh ? 1 : 0.8) * dim)
        .selectAll("path")
        .attr("d", r => path({type: "LineString", coordinates: r.coords}))
        .attr("stroke", r => COLORS[r.c])
        .attr("stroke-width", fresh ? 3.6 : 2);
    });

    gTop.selectAll("*").remove();
    if (selected && selected.y <= year) {
      const g = gTop.append("g");
      g.selectAll("path.h").data(selected.runs).join("path")
        .attr("d", r => path({type: "LineString", coordinates: r.coords}))
        .attr("stroke", "#020617").attr("stroke-width", 8);
      g.selectAll("path.c").data(selected.runs).join("path")
        .attr("d", r => path({type: "LineString", coordinates: r.coords}))
        .attr("stroke", r => COLORS[r.c]).attr("stroke-width", 4.5);
      const p = projection([selected.close.lon, selected.close.lat]);
      if (p) g.append("circle").attr("cx", p[0]).attr("cy", p[1]).attr("r", 8)
        .attr("stroke", "#fff").attr("stroke-width", 2.5).attr("fill", "none");
    }

    // Wide invisible strokes make thin tracks easy to tap
    gHit.selectAll("path").data(shown, d => d.i).join("path")
      .attr("d", s => path({type: "LineString", coordinates: s.pts.map(p => [p.lon, p.lat])}))
      .attr("stroke", "transparent").attr("stroke-width", 16)
      .style("cursor", "pointer")
      .on("click", (e, s) => select(selected === s ? null : s));

    out.value = year;
    slider.value = year;
    const n = shown.length;
    count.innerHTML = year === lastYear
      ? `<b>${n}</b> storms from 1851 to ${lastYear}`
      : `<b>${n}</b> storm${n === 1 ? "" : "s"} from 1851 to ${year}`;
  }

  function readout() {
    if (!selected) {
      read.innerHTML = `<b>Tap any track</b> (or a button above) to see how strong that storm was when it reached NYC.`;
      return;
    }
    const s = selected, c = s.close, d = new Date(Date.UTC(+s.dt.slice(0, 4), +s.dt.slice(4, 6) - 1, +s.dt.slice(6, 8)));
    const pk = s.peak;
    const peakTxt = pk.st === "HU" ? `<b>Category ${cat(pk.w)}</b>, ${mph(pk.w)} mph` : `${describe(pk.st, pk.w).replace(/<\/?b>/g, "")}, ${mph(pk.w)} mph`;
    read.innerHTML = `<b>${s.label}</b><br>Closest to NYC on ${months[d.getUTCMonth()]} ${d.getUTCDate()}, ${s.y}: ${describe(c.st, c.w)} with ${mph(c.w)} mph winds, about ${s.d} km (${Math.round(s.d * 0.6214)} mi) away.<br>Strongest anywhere on its path: ${peakTxt}.${s.note ? `<span class="u5h-note">${s.note}</span>` : ""}`;
  }

  function select(s) {
    selected = s;
    if (s && s.y > year) year = lastYear;
    sel.value = s ? String(s.i) : "";
    drawTracks();
    readout();
  }

  // ---------- Controls ----------
  slider.addEventListener("input", () => { stopPlay(); year = +slider.value; drawTracks(); });
  zoomBtn.onclick = () => {
    view = view === "atlantic" ? "nyc" : "atlantic";
    zoomBtn.setAttribute("aria-pressed", view === "nyc");
    zoomBtn.textContent = view === "nyc" ? "🌎 Whole Atlantic" : "🔍 Zoom to NYC";
    fit(view); drawBase(); drawTracks();
  };

  let timer = null, visible = true;
  function stopPlay() {
    if (timer) { clearInterval(timer); timer = null; }
    playBtn.textContent = "▶ Play";
  }
  function startPlay() {
    if (year >= lastYear) year = firstYear - 1;
    playBtn.textContent = "⏸ Pause";
    timer = setInterval(() => {
      if (!visible) return;           // pause quietly while scrolled away
      year += 1;
      drawTracks();
      if (year >= lastYear) stopPlay();
    }, reduceMotion ? 160 : 70);
  }
  playBtn.onclick = () => timer ? stopPlay() : startPlay();

  const io = new IntersectionObserver(([e]) => { visible = e.isIntersecting; });
  io.observe(wrap);
  invalidation.then(() => { io.disconnect(); stopPlay(); });

  drawBase();
  drawTracks();
  readout();
  return wrap;
}

## Anchor Phenomenon

> **It has felt like storms are getting worse. Does the data support that feeling, and will it continue?**
>
> Recent blizzard seasons buried the East Coast, and recent hurricane seasons, like the record 30 named storms of 2020, brought storms such as Maria that devastated Puerto Rico. This unit builds on Unit 4: if global temperatures keep rising, what happens to the storms that reach New York City?

## Unit Driving Question

> **Will there be more frequent and more intense severe storms in the future?**

**Performance task:** Write an **argument from evidence** about how storms will change in **frequency** and **intensity** as global temperatures continue to rise. For each type of storm you will:

1. **Identify** the independent and dependent variables in the question
2. **Gather evidence** and **develop a model** of how energy and matter flow in the storm system
3. **Argue** for a claim, address a counterclaim, and explain the limits of the climate models you used

## Unit Storyline

| Lesson | Question |
|---|---|
| [Unit Opening](unit5-opening.qmd) | Will there be more frequent and more intense severe storms in the future? |
| [Moon Phases (Optional)](unit5-moon-phases.qmd) | How does the Moon contribute to storm severity? |
| [Blizzards](unit5-blizzards.qmd) | How do severe winter storms form? What causes wind and precipitation? Can we make predictions about these weather phenomena? |
| [The Paths of Severe Storms](unit5-storm-paths.qmd) | How do severe winter storms form? What causes wind and precipitation? (Why do storms follow the paths they do?) |
| [Hurricanes](unit5-hurricanes.qmd) | How do hurricanes form? Why do hurricanes exhibit patterns in the time of year they occur? |
| [Unit Closing](unit5-closing.qmd) | How will storms change in our region as climate change continues? |

## What You'll Figure Out

By the end of this unit, you will be able to:

::: {.key-idea}
- 🌕 **Explain** how the Moon's position causes tides, and why a full-moon high tide made Sandy's flooding worse
- 🌬️ **Explain** how uneven heating causes air pressure differences, wind, and precipitation
- 🌨️ **Model** how warm and cold air masses meet to produce winter storms and blizzards
- 🗺️ **Analyze** how global wind patterns and the jet stream steer storms toward NYC
- 🌀 **Describe** how hurricanes draw energy from warm ocean water, and why they peak in late summer and fall
- 📊 **Use** historical storm data and climate projections to predict changes in storm frequency and intensity
- 📢 **Construct** an evidence-based argument, with a counterclaim, about future storms where you live
